entities.summary: Colonial military units composed of African Muslims were stationed in Besançon and the Franche-Comté from the 1870s to World War I to augment the French army and protect its frontiers during its conflicts with Germany. Large-scale immigration of Muslims to France began in the 1960s and 1970s. In 1981, the Center of Islam of the Franche-Comté was created, as the sunna association was formed in 1987. In 2010, Islam was the second largest religion in Besançon after Catholicism. According to a report by France Bleu Besançon in 2010, 15,000 Muslims live in Besançon and comprise about 13% of the city's population.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Al-Fath Mosque in Besançon represents a significant regional impact as it reflects the growing Muslim population in Western Europe, with approximately 15,000 Muslims residing in Besançon and comprising about 13% of the city's population. This demographic shift has contributed to the diversification of French society.
